raw_response:
I will still do it much like last year, only I will watch prices and cut nothing that can hurt yield. On my 18 mu, cotton is still my main crop, because I know it well and we have well water, so I am not afraid to hold fertilizer a bit higher on the cotton land. I only finished primary school, but after farming this many years I do look at the field condition, not just throw inputs blindly. If the land that carried cotton last year looks tired, I will not be stingy with nitrogen and potash there. Around here, if cotton is weak early, it never really catches up, so I will feed it enough, water 3 times if the season is normal, and spray 4 times because cotton pests are never light. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because that is what people around me use when they want steady ears. Maize grows fast, so I will put enough base fertilizer and then chase it once, with 2 waterings if rain does not come. Wheat I will keep on the better, flatter land because wheat shows quickly if fertilizer is short. I will use improved wheat seed, give it 3 waterings if water is available, and not save money on the first fertilizer. Family labor is not as full as before because some go out to work, so on the bigger pieces I will choose plough or rotary tillage that lets the work finish fast and clean. I would rather spend a little more on fertilizer and seed than lose yield and regret it later.
